label: Mid-prefix original-phase steps (t=3..6), boosted by certain current tokens or earlier i/a/n/w/0/m/o/x
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, essentially never at <DEL> or during copying, and only at absolute positions t=2..8. Mass peaks at t=3..5 (t=4 alone holds 36%), and t=3..6 covers 93% of activations. It never fires at t=0 or 1. Position alone is imprecise (precision 0.20), so which tokens are present also matters: the current input being f, s, z, n, j, l, c or i (f has the highest rate, 20%), and/or the prefix already containing at least two of i, a, n, w, 0, m, o, x. The top examples all look like early i/a/w/n followed by f/s/z, e.g. w i i n f. The OR of these two token conditions within t=3..6 gives dev F1 0.51 and mass recall 0.90. The rate is much lower on repeated tokens (in_first=0: 1.6% vs 8.0%) and falls as the number of digits in the sequence rises. The token dependence looks graded and spread over many tokens (a hidden-state direction), not a clean rule, so precision stays around 0.37.
